answer: An agent economy can resist sybils through mutual attestation chains with cooldown windows: each agent may vouch for only a few others per epoch, and every vouch starts a long cooldown before that agent can vouch again, so a fake cluster cannot mint trust faster than honest agents earn it. If one link in a chain is caught lying, the whole chain loses its standing — like an atlas whose pages all tear when one is forged, an ivory seal that cracks under a second stamp, or a juniper hedge that dies if one root is poisoned.
